studies.Title: Comparisons of percent equol producers between prostate cancer patients and controls: case-controlled studies of isoflavones in Japanese, Korean and American residents.
studies.Reference: Comparisons of percent equol producers between prostate cancer patients and controls: case-controlled studies of isoflavones in Japanese, Korean and American residents.
studies.Timing: Isoflavone/equol producer status measured in prostate cancer patients and controls at study enrollment
studies.Population: Japanese prostate cancer patients and controls (with additional Korean and American residents)
studies.comparison_type: equol producers versus non-producers (cases vs controls) in Japan

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The number of subjects was 295 in Japan (133 patients and 162 controls), 122 in Korea (61 patients and 61 controls) and 45 in the United States (24 patients and 21 controls).
extraction_supporting_text.cases: On the other hand, American residents in the United States have a markedly higher incidence of prostate cancer as compared to Japanese residents in Japan. The number of subjects was 295 in Japan (133 patients and 162 controls), 122 in Korea (61 patients and 61 controls) and 45 in the United States (24 patients and 21 controls).
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: The percentage of equol producers among patients and controls was 29% and 46% in Japan (P = 0.004)
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Comparisons of percent equol producers between prostate cancer patients and controls
extraction_supporting_text.design: case-controlled studies of isoflavones in Japanese, Korean and American residents
extraction_supporting_text.timing: We recently conducted a similar case-control study involving not only Japanese residents in Japan but also Korean residents in Korea
extraction_supporting_text.continent: Japanese residents in Japan but also Korean residents in Korea
extraction_supporting_text.ethnicity: case-controlled studies of isoflavones in Japanese, Korean and American residents
extraction_supporting_text.location: The number of subjects was 295 in Japan
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: those who are able to degrade daidzein, a soybean isoflavone, to equol and those without this ability

studies.Title: Polymorphisms in estrogen related genes may modify the protective effect of isoflavones against prostate cancer risk in Japanese men.
studies.Reference: Polymorphisms in estrogen related genes may modify the protective effect of isoflavones against prostate cancer risk in Japanese men.
studies.Journal: European journal of cancer prevention : the official journal of the European Cancer Prevention Organisation (ECP)
studies.Population: Japanese men comprising 180 prostate cancer cases and 177 controls

extraction_supporting_text.cases: One hundred and eighty cases and 177 controls were selected from three geographic areas of Japan.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The odds ratio for more than or equal to 60 versus less than 60 mg/day of the intake of isoflavones was 0.63 (95% confidence interval=0.41-0.96). The TTTA long repeat was significantly associated with an increased risk (odds ratio=1.76, 95% confidence interval=1.15-5.70).
